extraction.name: SWE-rebench
extraction.description: A public dataset comprising over 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks, suitable for reinforcement learning of SWE agents at scale. The dataset is constructed using a novel, automated, and scalable pipeline to continuously extract real-world interactive SWE tasks from diverse GitHub repositories.
extraction.license: Permissive licenses including MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-4-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, BSD-2-Clause, ISC, CC0-1.0, ZPL-2.1, and other manually verified permissive licenses
extraction.creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel (Nebius)
extraction.citeAs: Badertdinov et al., SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents, NeurIPS 2025 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is collected using a fully automated pipeline that downloads raw input data from GitHub Archive and GitHub. The pipeline downloads approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025, originating from over 30,000 repositories with permissive licenses where Python constitutes over 75% of the codebase. Issues are linked with pull requests that mention resolving them in their title or description.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Software Collection, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: GitHub Archive is used to collect detailed data about issues including issue description, discussion, linked pull requests, and metadata such as creation date and labels. Information about pull requests is also extracted, including their merge status, last commit, and discussions. GitHub repositories are cloned with their full commit histories to local storage.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Issues created before May 1, 2025. The benchmark subset includes tasks from issues created in 2025 (January-July 2025 for evaluation).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For each selected pull request, the overall patch is divided into two components: a solution patch, containing changes to non-test files intended to address the issue, and a test patch, comprising only changes to test files. Task instances are grouped by project versions inferred from git tag outputs, normalizing versions to major.minor format. For each version group, the base_commit of the pull request linked to the task instance with the most recent base_commit date is selected.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Multiple filtering steps are applied: (1) The issue must be from a Python repository with a permissive license, (2) The issue must be marked as resolved, (3) The PR must be merged into the main branch, (4) The PR must not be linked to multiple issues, (5) The issue description must be longer than 10 characters, (6) The PR must introduce or modify tests and include code changes beyond test files, (7) Changes must affect 1 to 15 files. After preliminary filtering, approximately 153,400 potential task instances remain. Additional filtering for the benchmark subset includes: clean test execution logs, no more than 3 files modified, total words in solution patch not exceeding 500, problem statement between 16 and 1000 words, English language, created in 2025, LLM-assessed difficulty less than 3, and 50 or fewer fail-to-pass tests.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: An LLM-based automated quality assessment is performed. A Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model is fine-tuned using human annotations from SWE-bench Verified to predict three binary quality labels: Issue Clarity (whether the GitHub issue description is sufficiently detailed), Task Complexity (estimated effort to resolve the issue), and Test Patch Correctness (whether tests accurately verify the intended fix). The model receives the issue description, canonical solution patch, and test patch as input and predicts each label independently.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For Task Complexity (100 high-score vs. 313 low-score examples in validation), the fine-tuned model achieved 81% accuracy and weighted F1-score of 0.82. For Test Patch Correctness (180 high-score vs. 233 low-score examples), the model achieved 67% accuracy (weighted F1: 0.65). For Issue Clarity (84 high-score vs. 329 low-score examples), it achieved 79% accuracy (weighted F1: 0.76). The LLM-generated labels are provided as metadata with each task instance.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three quality assessment labels per task instance: Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct model fine-tuned on SWE-bench Verified annotations for automated quality assessment
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset uses an automated pipeline for continuous supply of fresh tasks. The benchmark is continuously updated with new tasks to ensure decontamination. The leaderboard is publicly accessible at https://swe-rebench.com/leaderboard and is continuously updated with new model evaluations.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to accelerate open-source research and improve the reliability and performance of LLM-based software engineering agents. However, the progress brings potential risks such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities. The authors believe that fostering openness, decontaminated evaluations, and rigorous benchmarking practices helps mitigate these concerns.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The fully automated pipeline may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue, leading to lower absolute success rates compared to manually curated benchmarks. The initial release is limited exclusively to Python, restricting immediate applicability to other language ecosystems. Some failure modes include flaky tests with external API calls or floating-point precision issues, lack of interactivity during installation for some projects, and unpinned and obsolete dependencies in older repositories. The automated quality assessment cannot fully replicate nuanced human judgment.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training and benchmarking LLM-based agents in diverse executable environments, particularly suitable for reinforcement learning-based approaches. Use cases include: Training software engineering agents, Testing and evaluation of agent capabilities, Validation of model performance on real-world SWE tasks, and Fine-tuning open-source models for software engineering tasks.
